# IdeaVim fixtures this host does not match yet.
#
# Generated by VimFixtureReplayTest, which writes the current list to
# build/fixture-failures.txt with the difference for each one, and a header saying how many were
# harvested and why the rest were not. To update this file, read that one and copy the names across
# - never edit a name by hand to make the build pass.
#
# 1613 of the 1615 harvested fixtures pass, and both of the two left name an IntelliJ action.
#
# The corpus has grown from 1,047 to 1,615 in three steps, and every one of them was the harness
# looking at less of `src/test` than it thought.
#
# It only found backtick-quoted test names, so IdeaVim's 578 plainly-named tests were *invisible*
# rather than refused - they never reached the skip counts either, so the reported yield was
# measuring what could be parsed out of what could be seen. It only read a method whose body
# *started* with `doTest`, so a method that bound its text first, or called `doTest` more than once,
# gave up everything but the first call. And it skipped the 1,039 `doTest` calls under `/extension/`
# wholesale, on the grounds that "the extension tests need plugins this host has not ported" -
# twenty-two of the twenty-four are ported now.
#
# What kept the extension tests out after that was where their setup lives: `enableExtensions`, and
# the `let` that has to precede it, are in `setUp` - a *different method*, and the harness only ever
# looked at the one it was in. `enableExtensions` sets the extension's toggle option, which is what
# `:set surround` does, and `set <name>` was `E518` here until the extension options were
# registered; these fixtures could not have been replayed before that was fixed either. 461 of the
# 1,039 are `matchit`, which is not ported and is not going to be.
#
# Twenty of the 568 failed. Seven were real gaps in this host and all seven are fixed. Two were
# order dependence, which was the worst thing this found: `VimSearchGroupBase` keeps
# `lastPatternTrailing` and three of its neighbours in a `protected companion object` - one per
# process, however many search groups exist - so `n` after `:s` inherited the `3` from a `/and/3`
# two fixtures earlier and answered three lines below the match it had correctly found. The replay
# resets the engine between fixtures now, the way IdeaVim's own `VimTestCase.setUp` does. Every
# fixture had been replayed into whatever its neighbour left behind, so a pass meant less than it
# looked like it did.
#
# The other eleven were one gap and are fixed: `.` did not repeat what an extension did, because
# repeating an extension mapping means running *the handler* again rather than a command, and this
# host's copy of `RepeatChangeAction` had only the command branch. The body is `repeatLastChange` in
# `vim-engine` now and both hosts share it.
#
# Before believing an entry in this file, check that the fixture passes in the plugin. Two of them
# did not: `search in one time from select mode` sat here as "expected [81], actual [82]" when
# IdeaVim's own caret is at 82, and `repeat command with execution of ij action` had a reason
# written against it that was not why it failed. Both are `@Disabled` over there, and the harness
# now skips those.

# --- Two IntelliJ actions, which this host has no equivalent of.
#
# `ideajoin` is IntelliJ's smart join, a language feature this host cannot have: `VjJ` with the
# option set joins the way the language wants rather than the way Vim does.
#
# `partial Action mapping` types `X(EditorToggleCase)` into a half-declared `<Action>` mapping. The
# mapping machinery works - nothing is inserted as literal text, which is what this entry used to
# claim - and `EditorToggleCase` is an IntelliJ action id with no VS Code command behind it. There
# is no toggle-case command; `editor.action.transformToUppercase` and its lowercase twin are the
# whole of what VS Code offers.
